newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines says credit growth slows down in April.
newsitem.headline: Philippines says credit growth slows down in April.

text.p: The Philippine Central Bank said on Wednesday the growth of loans extended by commercial banks slowed down to 34.7 percent in April from 37.4 percent a month ago.

"This should further confirm our assurances that the previous rapid growth in domestic credits ... will stabilise. We foresee therefore more favourable prospects for both sustained higher growth and lower inflation this year," Central Bank governor Gabriel Singson said in a statement.
Domestic credit has been accelerating since 1992, peaking at 54.5 percent in September last year.
Credits to private sector decelerated to 36.5 percent from 36.9 percent in March, while loans to the public sector slowed down to 26.8 percent from 39.5 percent.
"We maintain that the robust expansion in outstanding loans of commercial banks as an indispensable ingredient to sustained growth," Singson said.

Loans to most sectors have been tempered, but loans given to financial institutions, real estate and business services remained at a high of 62.6 percent. Loans to the sector grew by 97.2 percent for the whole of last year.

The manufacturing sector remained the biggest borrower, cornering 30 percent of the outstanding loans of the banks. It was followed by the financial institutions, real estate and business services, 24 percent.

"We look at 1997 as another high growth year. Therefore, we would expect continued high demand for credit although the growth could stabilise at levels comparable to the growth in GNP, inflation and the increased rate of financial deepening," Singson added.
